leads.candidate: Remaining register trees in the Topkapı/Gülhane sub-cluster not yet delivered: an At Kestanesi/Aesculus hippocastanum horse chestnut (OBJECTID 399, 173yr, 41.011526/28.978794), an Akdeniz Servisi/Cupressus sempervirens cypress (OBJECTID 420, 365yr, 41.011732/28.983386), a second Çitlenbik (OBJECTID 409, 238yr, 41.009116/28.981254), two more Porsuk yews (OBJECTIDs 403/404, 240/264yr, same Topkapı 4th courtyard as ist_014)
leads.why_a_lead: 2026-08-09 deepen pass delivered 3 of the strongest candidates from this cluster (ist_012 London Plane, ist_013 Nettle Tree, both Gülhane Park; ist_014 European Yew, Topkapı 4th courtyard), each with a genuine second source (IBB's konusanagac.com dedicated pages for the first two, monumentaltrees.com's independent Topkapı-palace tree list for the yew). The rest were checked and still fail the two-independent-source bar: the horse chestnut's only non-register lead (an Ittifak Gazetesi piece citing registration number 'AVR.AA.1065') traces back to avrupaanitagaclar.com's own numbering scheme, which is compromised and not usable, so effectively still single-sourced; the cypress has no dedicated konusanagac.com page and no clean girth match against monumentaltrees.com's several unmeasured/mismatched Topkapı cypress entries (register girth 4.31m vs monumentaltrees' matched entry of 2.79m, not the same tree); OBJECTID 409's Çitlenbik sits about 350m from the delivered OBJECTID 400 and has no page of its own on konusanagac.com. A future pass could try a Turkish news search specifically for 'Gülhane Parkı at kestanesi' beyond what this pass found, or check konusanagac.com's mobile app / full ozel-konusan-agaclar list directly (site loads in a browser session; DNS to konusanagac.com fails from a plain curl/WebFetch sandbox, so this needs an interactive session, same as the monumentaltrees.com 403).
leads.caution: Several of these records' own 'url' field points at avrupaanitagaclar.com, which is compromised as of 2026-08-08 and now serves unrelated gambling content, not tree data. Do not use it as a source, and treat any secondary source (news, blogs) that quotes an 'AVR.AA.####' registration number as ultimately traceable to that same compromised site rather than independent. Use the anitagaclar.gov.tr detail pages / arcgis feature service fields directly instead; anitagaclar.gov.tr itself is fine and fetchable (curl with a browser user-agent works), but note it is the SAME underlying government database as the ArcGIS layer, not a second independent source of its own, and its free-text story field has documented content-pairing bugs.

leads.candidate: Register tree at 41.01434, 28.957055, Doğu Çınarı, 268 years (OBJECTID 434), near Süleymaniye
leads.why_a_lead: Roughly 1km west of the main Topkapı/Gülhane sub-cluster and about 600-900m from Süleymaniye Mosque's own coordinates; could plausibly be one of Süleymaniye külliyesi's courtyard plane trees, which multiple sources describe generically (courtyard 'shaded by historic plane trees since the 15th century', citing Evliya Çelebi) but never individually name or date. Not verified this pass: no independent source ties this specific register point to Süleymaniye by name, and the courtyard-tree sources found give no age for any single specimen there.

leads.candidate: Register tree at 41.010664, 28.965437, Doğu Çınarı, 322 years (OBJECTID 413)
leads.why_a_lead: Sits roughly 70m from the already-published Hüseyin Avni Dede Plane (ist_003, Sahaflar Çarşısı entrance, Beyazıt), almost certainly the same physical tree recorded independently in this national registry with a different age figure (322 vs ist_003's sourced 375). Not a new entry; recorded here so a future pass does not re-discover it and mistake it for a second, separate tree at Beyazıt.

leads.candidate: Beyazıt Mosque courtyard plane / execution-witness tree mentioned in Hürriyet's Istanbul-planes survey
leads.why_a_lead: Hürriyet's roundup of century-old Istanbul planes lists a 'Beyazıt Mosque courtyard plane, historic significance as execution site witness' alongside the Sahaflar Çarşısı tree. Given Beyazıt Mosque and the Sahaflar Çarşışı entrance sit metres apart on the same square, and both carry an execution-tree legend (Cellat Çınarı), this is very likely the SAME tree as ist_003 described from a slightly different angle, not confirmed as distinct this pass. Worth a five-minute check on a future pass before treating it as new.

blocked.candidate: Yeniçeriler Çınarı (Janissaries' Plane), Topkapı Palace First Courtyard
blocked.reason: Dead. Confirmed by istanbulansiklopedisi.org (Istanbul Encyclopedia) and multiple Turkish news pieces: began drying after 1900, reduced to a stump by 1930, propped on a concrete support to keep the fragment from collapsing. Already reflected honestly in the Istanbul city file's own intro paragraph; must never be added as a live collectible entry.

blocked.candidate: Kanlı Çınar / Vakvak Ağacı (Bloody Plane / Vakvak Tree), Sultanahmet/Atmeydanı between Hagia Sophia and the Sultan Ahmed Mosque
blocked.reason: Dead and gone. Historically used to hang the bodies of 30 executed officials in 1655 during a Janissary revolt; the tree dried out over the following centuries, its protective chain was removed to the City Museum, and a German Fountain (Alman Çeşmesi) now stands on the site. No living tree to point to.
Removed on the order of Sultan Abdülhamid II after it was used for the 1876 execution of Binbaşı Çerkes Hasan Bey. Long gone, no living specimen.

blocked.candidate: Gülhane Parkı 'Ceviz Ağacı' (Nazım Hikmet's walnut tree)
blocked.reason: Not an ancient or even old tree, and the popular legend behind it is false. Multiple Turkish fact-check outlets (Teyit, Malumatfuruş) and the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality itself confirm the poem 'Ceviz Ağacı' was written in Balçık, Bulgaria in 1957, not under a walnut tree in Gülhane Park with Piraye. The municipality only planted an actual walnut tree in the park in 2006, after discovering there had never been one there. Fails the age and genuineness bar entirely; not a collectible ancient tree under any reading.
